title: Omar bin al-Khattab and the Young Bedouin
logline: A young Bedouin condemned for a killing asks three days to settle his orphan brother; a stranger, Abu Dharr, stakes his own life on his return, the youth runs back through the heat at the last moment, and the dead man sons forgive him.
moral: Kept promises, generous trust and mercy keep each other alive: loyalty answered by honour, honour answered by pardon.
tone: Serious and warm court drama with suspense (the sinking sun) and release; restrained staging, light human comedy only in the bystanders who avoid Umar gaze. No comic treatment of the killing or of the companions.

beats.summary: Two brothers drag a young Bedouin into Umar council.
They accuse him of killing their father.
Flashback: the orchard owner kills his prized horse with a stone.
In rage he throws the same stone back; the man dies; horror at his own hand.
He asks three days for his orphan brother and promises to return.
Who will vouch? Everyone looks away; a second of silence.
He points at a stranger: Abu Dharr.
Abu Dharr vouches and later sits in the accused place.
Third day, sinking sun, empty door; the room fears for Abu Dharr.
Blood money is offered and refused.
The youth appears over the dunes, running through the heat.
He came back so loyalty would not vanish; Abu Dharr vouched so honour would not vanish.
The brothers forgive him; he sinks to his knees.
So that mercy would not vanish: the third tag completes the row.
They gently decline the treasury money and raise the youth to his feet.

subtitles.ar: تروي حكاية قديمة أن شابين جاءا إلى مجلس الخليفة عمر بن الخطاب،|وأمسكا بفتى بدوي يتهمانه بقتل أبيهما.|طلب عمر منهما شرح الأمر،|فقالا إن والدهما خرج إلى بستانه، فمات هناك بسبب هذا الشاب.
subtitles.en: An old tale says two brothers|brought a young Bedouin before Caliph Umar,|accusing him of killing their father in his orchard.|Umar asked for an account.

subtitles.ar: أقر الفتى بأن الرجل مات بسببه،|وقال إن ناقة له دخلت البستان،|فقتل صاحب البستان فرسًا ثمينًا كان معه بحجر.
subtitles.en: The youth admitted causing the man's death.|One of his camels had entered the orchard,|and its owner had killed the youth's valuable horse with a stone.

subtitles.ar: غضب الفتى، فرمى الرجل بالحجر نفسه فمات.|اعترف بفعله،|وحكم عمر بالقصاص كما تروي الحكاية.
subtitles.en: Enraged, the youth threw the same stone at the man and killed him.|He admitted his act,|and Umar ruled that retaliation was due, as the tale relates.

subtitles.ar: طلب الفتى مهلة ثلاثة أيام؛|فقد ترك أبوه مالًا لأخ صغير، ولا يعرف موضعه أحد سواه.|وعد بالعودة بعدما يطمئن على أخيه.
subtitles.en: The youth requested three days:|his father had left money for a younger brother, and only he knew where it was.|He promised to return after making arrangements for the child.

subtitles.ar: سأل عمر من يضمن عودة المتهم.|نظر الشاب إلى الحاضرين واختار أبا ذر، مع أنه لم يعرفه من قبل.|قبل أبو ذر أن يكون كفيلًا عنه،|فأذن الخليفة للشاب بالمغادرة ثلاثة أيام.
subtitles.en: Umar asked for a guarantor.|The youth chose Abu Dharr, a man he had never met.|Abu Dharr accepted the responsibility,|and the accused was allowed to leave.

subtitles.ar: انقضت الأيام واقترب موعد الحكم، ولم يظهر البدوي.|خاف الناس أن يتحمل أبو ذر العقوبة بدلًا منه،|وأصر ابنا القتيل أولًا على القصاص.|حاول بعض الحاضرين إقناعهما بقبول التعويض، لكنهما رفضا.
subtitles.en: Three days passed without the Bedouin.|The gathering feared Abu Dharr would be punished in his place,|while the dead man’s sons|initially refused compensation.

subtitles.ar: في اللحظات الأخيرة عاد الشاب متعبًا من شدة الحر،|وأعلن أنه سلّم أخاه الصغير إلى أخواله وأخبرهم بمكان المال.|قال إنه رجع كيلا يقال إن الوفاء اختفى من الناس،|وأوضح أبو ذر أنه ضمنه كيلا تختفي المروءة.
subtitles.en: At the last moment the youth returned, exhausted by heat.|He had entrusted his brother and the money to relatives.|He came back to keep his promise;|Abu Dharr explained why he had trusted him.

subtitles.ar: تأثر ابنا الرجل بوفاء الشاب وشجاعة أبي ذر،|فأعلنا العفو عن قاتل أبيهما حتى لا يقال إن الرحمة اختفت.|عرض عمر تعويضًا من بيت المال، لكنهما رفضاه.|وتنتهي الرواية باختيار العفو بعد نزاع مؤلم.
subtitles.en: Moved by the youth’s honesty and Abu Dharr’s generosity,|the brothers forgave him.|They refused public compensation,|and the tale ended with mercy instead of further bloodshed.

owner_questions: SCRIPT: the English translation is a condensed version of the Arabic in P1, P5, P6, P7 and P8 (for example the father going out to his orchard, the three days of leave, the attendees urging compensation, "so that it would not be said that loyalty / mercy had vanished" are in the Arabic only); both are kept verbatim.

Caliph Umar and Abu Dharr are companions of the Prophet: the plan shows them as plain, dignified Library figures with faces (Umar without crown or throne, on a simple bench); confirm, or ask for a no-face treatment (seen from behind or as bright silhouettes).

Violence is softened: both stone hits are hidden by a 2-frame white flash, the horse lies down with closed eyes, the owner sinks behind his wall and only his turban rolls out; no blood and no body. Default kept.

Invented lettering (not in the script): HE KILLED OUR FATHER!, I DID IT., A LIFE FOR A LIFE, 3 DAYS?, ONLY I KNOW, WHO WILL VOUCH?, ABU DHARR, A STRANGER!, I VOUCH!, JUSTICE!, NO!, HE CAME BACK!, WE FORGIVE! and the three tags LOYALTY, HONOUR, MERCY; default is to use them all (19 items with the title, the LATER card and THE END).
Title card text is "UMAR AND THE YOUNG BEDOUIN" (the file title spells Omar / Badawi); default follows the English subtitle spelling Umar.

Additions beyond the script: the guarantor sits in the accused place while waiting, a second purse is added to the offer, the youth offers his wrists on return, and a white dove crosses the doorway at the end; default is to keep them.
The Arabic "ناقة له ... فرسًا ثمينًا كان معه" is staged as his she-camel straying into the orchard and the owner killing the youth horse (his, the youth) with a stone; confirm this reading.
implementation_notes: Start from Library/template; one scene file. Set LIFE.t = t each frame so all figures blink; give noBlink during the held silences (73.9-75.0, 148.0-149.6).
All cue times are word starts from timeline.md; define them as w(p, n) from timing.json and keep the literal values in comments.

Hall: const H = palaceHall(ctx, {variant: 'palace', wall: 'ochre', throne: false, outside: drawDesert, t}); read H.door, H.floor and H.lamps; place Umar with person({y: benchTop, sit: 1, seat: 'bench'}) on the scene-drawn bench. Floor sitters use sit: 1, seat: 'floor'.
Depth order in the hall: bystander (back), seated men, Umar, then the standing group, then the door light shaft overlay (multiply-like pale yellow at alpha 0.25).
Brothers are never in unison: brotherB = brotherA delayed by stagger(1) (3 to 5 frames) with 70 % amplitude; this difference is also their character.
The three tags are panel-space S.label boxes at y 110 (x 190, 500, 810 after 164.22; before that left-aligned from x 150); they persist from their pop time to the end. weekDots hides at 129.36.
Flashback (S4, S5) is drawn through taleZoom inside the cloud clip, then full panel; the dream wash goes on top; panel-only shake at 38.38 and 43.08.

Stone arcs: 37.83-38.38 from the owner hand (690, 720) to (270, 745), apex 120 above; 42.1-43.08 from the youth hand (240, 730) to the wall top (700, 790), apex 150 above. The flash frames are the two frames at each arrival.
Sun in the doorway: y keyed 640 (95.0) to 760 (116.0), then 790 by 166; outside tint via dayCycle(u).warm. After 161.4 set lampsLit and let the hall wall warm slightly with mixHex.
Sound: six effects only (7.65 thud, 24.65 pop, 39.5 thud, 52.6 thud, 115.7 whoosh, 167.3 chime), SND master 0.6, all inside listed pauses or after the last word.
Subtitles: write chunks_ar.txt and chunks_en.txt from the subtitles array (| marks) and verify by program against the script.
warnings: Depiction of Umar and Abu Dharr is sensitive for part of the audience (see owner_questions); the staging works unchanged if they must be shown from behind or as silhouettes, except the eye-contact beat at 75.9-77.2, which would need to be carried by the youth eyes and a head turn.
The hall is crowded (8 figures in 1000 units): keep the seated row at s 0.78 and check stills at 8.9, 78.1 and 149.6 that no head is covered and every face is above the caption panel.

The palaceHall dais and throne defaults must be switched off or narrowed; check the option names (dais, throne: false) in sets/towns.js before staging and measure the door anchor rather than trusting the numbers here.
The front-facing person cannot show a profile throw: both throws read through arm angles (aR), body tip and the stone arc; test at phone size.
Lettering is near the limit (19 items with the LATER card). If any is cut, cut I DID IT. and JUSTICE! first; the three tags and WE FORGIVE! carry the moral.
Narration is dense with few pauses, so only six sound effects are planned; do not add more inside sentences.
